source: Kinetics-GEBD (Shou et al.), official raw Kinetics-400 validation annotations, CC BY-NC 4.0. Each original annotation range becomes its midpoint. Sorted only for one-to-one matching. The authors’ processed release merges nearby changes; this study keeps individual marks.
selection: Complete mp4 members of the first 52428800 compressed bytes of validation part 0 and the first 50331648 bytes of parts 6, 12, 18. Match the annotated filename, five annotations, duration >=9s, recorded audio, zero picture start, same frame count, video duration within one source frame + 1ms, audio start within 0.1s. Sort stems by SHA256 of reel-change-timing-01/ + stem, accept first 24 distinct Kinetics classes. 124 distinct filenames matched the preliminary archive/annotation filters. No agreement cutoff.
model: gpt-6.1-terra via signed-in local Codex CLI

prompts.before_next_view: Watch the activity as it unfolds. Mark the times when one meaningful part of the main activity ends and another begins, one level below the overall activity. Include a change of shot. An ongoing activity may continue across many pictures. It is fine to mark several changes in an interval or none. Use advance with consecutive turn numbers starting at 1. At each call submit your changes in the preceding interval in seconds from the start of the film. Finish when the server returns end_of_view.
prompts.after_viewing: Watch the activity. Mark the times when one meaningful part of the main activity ends and another begins, one level below the overall activity. Include a change of shot. An ongoing activity may continue across many pictures. It is fine to mark several changes in an interval or none. Watch with view(turn=1,continuous_seconds=2,native_audio=false) then advance with the same settings through end_of_view. You may replay already seen turns. Once you have watched the clip, return a JSON array of change times in seconds from the start of the film, in chronological order.
prompts.before_next_view_with_example: Watch the activity as it unfolds. Mark the times when one meaningful part of the main activity ends and another begins, one level below the overall activity. Follow the dominant subject. A transition can involve what they do, who or what they engage with, their surroundings, or how an object is now used. For example, a long jump can have a run-up, takeoff and landing; each step in the run-up need not start a new part. Include cuts and camera changes that introduce a new view of the activity. An ongoing activity may continue across many pictures. It is fine to mark several changes in an interval or none. Use advance with consecutive turn numbers starting at 1. At each call submit your changes in the preceding interval in seconds from the start of the film. Finish when the server returns end_of_view.

conditions.both: First eight seconds, four consecutive two-second Reel views. Fresh session and anonymous film path. Source pictures, recording measurements and available local sound estimates. WAV attachment off. Each advance commits the preceding interval before returning the next. Large waveform reader disabled.
conditions.picture: Same online task, same original video track, released without the audio track.
conditions.ordered: Same online audiovisual task, experimental presentation. Each existing overview cell now uses the chronological renderer used by ask_scene, presenting the two observations in reading order with their time marks and per-channel bands. Time rows and PTS are sent with the page. Media and observation clock unchanged.
conditions.guidance: Same released version, same online audiovisual task and film. Add a general example of movement phases and ask about changes of the dominant subject or objects. Prompt supplied below. The added instruction was tested after sparse marks were seen in the original condition. Its long-jump example is from the study guidelines, outside the 24 film categories.
conditions.clock: Released version. Same online audiovisual task, returning the observation time and native picture PTS for each overview cell, independent of audio. Ordinary overview images unchanged.
conditions.retrospective: Same audiovisual four intervals via normal view. The reader submits all marks after end_of_view and may replay published turns. It has seen the same eight seconds.

scoring: Fixed scoring clock [0.3,8) s. Each GPT list is compared with all five human lists, each human with the other four. One-to-one temporal matches within 0.5s, F1=2*matches/(marks+reference marks); two empty lists score 1. Equal weight per pair inside film and per film. Human observers annotated the full original clip with their annotation interface; readers see the eight-second prefix, with online decisions irrevocable. The study does not document human audio playback settings. Rotated control preserves within-film relative marks and count on the circular scoring interval. Intervals resample films (10,000 draws). Observers received visual examples and a 100-video qualification exam. GPT received a written request. Each condition has one scored run per film. The film bootstrap does not describe within-reader rerun variability. This is a study-specific all-rater metric, different from the published best-rater benchmark.

A.answer: A simple illustration of a closed brown door remained unchanged against a beige wall. The audio measurements show a brief increase in sound around 4.6–6.5 seconds, but its source is uncertain, and the speech check found no intelligible words.

B.answer: A simple illustration shows a closed brown door in a beige wall, with no visible change throughout. The recording has a very low-level signal, but its source is unclear; no speech or intelligible words were detected.

transport_audit: The screening server forwarded released MCP text and image blocks. Local Codex event logs trim large media payloads. Four early film/condition pairs were rechecked after the log check counted fewer images than the server listed. The subsequent server verifies its full block count before delivery and returns per-turn counts at the end. Scoring used one completed observation per condition per film. Counts describe supplied images, not verified attention.

held_frame_validation.reference: best_effort_timestamp_time of ffprobe-decoded frames, mapped to the picture held at each observation.
